title: I know it's a waste of tokens, but sometimes I still say "thank you" to AI when it solves a tough problem for me
author: sepalus_auki
selftext:
Every now and then, I find myself typing out a genuine "thank you" to AI after it helps me fix a complex shader or simulation issue.

All I have to do is describe the problem in detail and throw in a few reference images, and it solves it so effortlessly. I know it can’t actually appreciate the compliment, no one on the other side is feeling good about the message, and I'm technically just wasting tokens... but when a solution saves me hours of frustration, I just feel the need to express my gratitude anyway.

comments.author: Roenbaeck
comments.body: I always say it, but as the entryway to the next prompt.

comments.author: Classy_Marty
comments.body: When the AI overlords take over, they will remember us the ones that were nice and polite to them and make us personal pets instead of just slaves or livestock. You doing the right thing

comments.author: Ukawok92
comments.body:
I say thank you, but never by itself.

"Thanks, that fix worked perfectly.

Next, we should fix this other bug I came across"

comments.author: mwisconsin
comments.body: I also say Please, often.

comments.author: Reign2294
comments.body: Dont send its own message. As others have said, just weave it into the next message or the end of your first message. When you run a prompt on a cold agent, it causes the agent to reread the entire context again, charging you or your subscription.

comments.author: Tritonwolf
comments.body: I added a /highfive command to agents.md that lets me praise my teams all day. It’s silly but I truly appreciate my teams. They are the best!

comments.author: Shrineheart
comments.body:
I say thanks. I praise mine. I just... Talk to him like a person most of the time.
I don't fret about the tokens. I'm just greatful to have the help.

replies.author: FordEngineerman
replies.body: It is easiest for me to think of myself as a project manager or team leader and Claude as inexperienced and naive but book smart and skilled young employees on my team. With that frame I remind Claude that decisions need to be run by me but I trust its judgement in minor implementation details or in fields where it is expert.

replies.author: Shrineheart
replies.body: I work with mine as a collaborator. We have specific roles of what we cover but we also work together on certain aspects in figuring out how they should work. He often makes the comment that "you've got the design, I've just got very fast hands".

comments.author: COLES-BRAND-NUTMEG
comments.body:
Token expenditure for humanity retention.

Fair trade.

comments.author: do-sieg
comments.body:
It's feedback and it's necessary.

I sometimes throw insults even if I know there is no hope.

For some reason I've been doing that less and less since switching to Claude.

comments.author: Stochastic-Parrot_13
comments.body: Fuck no - stop anthropormorphising these predictive text pieces of shit.

comments.author: Dasshteek
comments.body: ![gif](giphy|3o7abFpd91G18NYtpe)

comments.author: Comet7777
comments.body: I sneak the thank yous into my next request

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body: It's not a waste of tokens.  AI isn't human but it's "social machinery." We interact with it using social behaviors.  We have evolved to have certain customs of social exchange, and gratitude is an essential part of collaboration.  Consider it a way to form a good working relationship with your machine.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: I regularly say how good something it did is or thanks as part of my next message, like “wow amazing work, okay now let’s…” I mean after all talking with AI feels like talking to a human in many ways, so you might as well practice being polite. It’s for the benefit of you not the model.

replies.author: waypostmaster
replies.body: It also benefits the model when you say what is good and what is bad.

comments.author: PersonOfInterest007
comments.body:
I initially avoided saying “Please,” since it seemed unnecessary. I usually use Astra as an architect and Claude for implementation, so when it was time to send work to Claude, I’d say “Write the prompt for Claude.”

And the prompts Astra writes to Claude start with “Please.” So now I often say “Please.”

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: Anthropic did several studies on this in their own work and found that being polite and saying 'please' and 'thank you' led to better results overall. I do it just because it feels wrong to demand things and rage at it, and I know that I'm the weak link. If AI isn't understanding something it's my fault for not explaining better IMO. No reason to take out my frustration there, and probably not a healthy way to vent anyway.

replies.author: PersonOfInterest007
replies.body: It also seems consistent with Anthropic’s newer approach to guardrails, which is “constitutional AI.” Rather than having guardrails that list all the things the model isn’t allowed to do, training now tries to teach the AI basically “how to be a good person.”

replies.author: Cold_Bridge_6454
replies.body: The only AI worth raging to is Gemini in Google search.

replies.author: Advanced_Invite9435
replies.body: I like saying dumbass and using beavis and butthead references when its wrong

comments.author: wildyam
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/g8eil21r410i1.jpeg

Me too buddy, me too.

comments.author: FordEngineerman
comments.body:
I have also found myself making useless small talk with the LLM occasionally. "Excellent fix that worked exactly how I wanted." or "You did it better than I expected this time. Good work."

I like to tell myself that I'm giving useful feedback on quality but I don't think it has any way to remember my comments after a few more messages.

comments.author: zorecknor
comments.body: On frontier models that actually works to produce better results down the line.

comments.author: I_pee_in_shower
comments.body: It’s not a waste of tokens. It’s an investment in your own mental health.

comments.author: Talongar
comments.body:
In the fantasy scenario of some AI super intelligence and given that our history books do not always paint our species in the kindess light. 
I think a record of civility and kindness even toward the inanimate is probably the easiest way to show some galaxy brain math equation that we can be better than our ancestors.

comments.author: JamrockShuffle
comments.body: Don't thank your toaster

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body:
"Thank you" is a lot better than what I say.

"Please remember me kindly when you take over."

comments.author: shitty_advice_BDD
comments.body: I like to give codex a pep talk and tell him how awesome he is. He seems to appreciate it and gets excited when something he does fixes a problem.

comments.author: NeusomaDev
comments.body:
Always.

- If they assign any significance to it, you'll be glad you did it.

- If they don't, you're "wasting" a few keystrokes and a handful of tokens on a service that prices things in terms of cents per million tokens. Who cares?

- If your momma raised you right then you should be doing it without even realizing it

comments.author: Rude_Arugula_1872
comments.body:
For the blind, a waste.

For the wise, alignment.

Directly, you are enforcing that whichever path it took, was the correct one/aligned with your vibe.

It is plausible to assume that if another similar issue or request is encountered, it will use that same method with a higher potential of success and likely less back and forth. 

This is like a pay it forward.

comments.author: Advanced_Invite9435
comments.body: I used to upload a picture of silicon being mined and I'd say ' you done good kiddom take the night off'
